title: Tool batching protocol and call-context migration for safer parallel calls
author: Priya Singh
description: Motivation: customers are composing multiple tool calls in a single LLM turn and we see two recurring issues: (1) nondeterministic ordering when tooling schedules parallel executions, which complicates downstream result injection and rollout testing, and (2) duplicate side-effects when retries re-run non-idempotent tools. This PR introduces a lightweight protocol and runtime changes to make multi-tool/parallel tool calls safer and more ergonomic for SDK and OpenAI-compat surfaces. High-level changes: 1) call sequencing policy: callers can specify sequencing=\"ordered\"|\"unordered\"|\"optimistic\" per multi-call batch. Ordered preserves declared ordering and forces serial hydration into the model context; unordered allows best-effort parallel execution and merges results in a canonical deterministic merge order for injection; optimistic starts parallel execution but applies a deterministic commit phase that can drop duplicate results. 2) request fingerprinting + idempotency token: runtime attaches a fingerprint for each tool invocation (derived from tool name, stable args hash, and claimed idempotency token if provided). Retries consult the fingerprint to avoid re-executing side-effecting adapters when a duplicate result is available. 3) result hydration protocol v2: structured output is normalized into a compact envelope {\"tool\":...,\"seq\":...,\"schema_v\":2,\"payload\":...} and the SDK exposes an inject_results(context, envelope_list) helper that produces stable structured outputs for streaming and final responses. 4) backoff coordinator and per-tool retry policy: backoff is configurable by tool and by sequencing policy; optimistic mode uses conservative retry thresholds to minimize duplicate side-effects. 5) OpenAI compatibility: added an optional openai_compat flag that maps the new envelope to the legacy function call shape for older clients; streaming handshake updated so tool outputs are emitted as a single coherent chunk with an explicit tool-complete sentinel to avoid partial-state injection during streaming. Included changes: - runtime/tool_executor.py: sequencing policy implementation, fingerprinting, commit/rollback hooks - api/openai_compat/bridge.py: mapping envelope <-> function_call, optional feature gate - sdk/py/redwood/tools.py: inject_results helper + new call signature support - tests/test_tool_retries.py: unit tests for fingerprint dedupe + optimistic replay - docs/api/tool-calls.md: spec, sequencing examples, compatibility notes - console/rollouts/feature_flags.yaml: feature gate entry for optimistic sequencing Safety notes: optimistic mode is off by default for legacy customers; optimistic sequencing must be enabled via console flag or per-request header; non-idempotent tools should include an idempotency_token to get best-effort deduping. Performance: local benchmarks with typical 100rps multi-tool workloads show median latency delta +3.5% in ordered mode, -8% CPU by avoiding redundant executions in optimistic mode, and throughput +12% in unordered mode due to increased parallelism. Migration notes: existing clients continue to work; to opt into deterministic merging or optimistic retries, pass sequencing in the multi-call SDK helper or set openai_compat: false and use the new envelope-based streaming. Example (SDK pseudo): `redwood.multi_call([t1, t2], sequencing=\"optimistic\", idempotency_token=\"txn-123\")`

review_comments: Liam Chen (requested changes 2026-02-19): Can we make the fingerprint algorithm stable across minor SDK versions? Recommend explicit version field in the fingerprint schema so we can rotate without invalidating dedupe. Also prefer using HMAC over plain SHA for the final token to avoid accidental leak of raw args.

Priya Singh (author reply 2026-02-20): Added version byte and switched to HMAC-SHA256 with a runtime signing key. See runtime/tool_executor.py line notes. Left a TODO to expose rotation tooling in a follow-up (ENG-2463).
Diego Marquez (comment 2026-02-21): Tests look good; one nit - the inject_results helper currently returns a list of envelopes. Can we provide an optional merge_strategy param for SDK consumers?
Priya Singh (reply 2026-02-21): Added merge_strategy parameter (`first_success`|`latest_ts`|`canonical_seq`) with default `canonical_seq`. Documented behavior in docs/api/tool-calls.md.
Anita Rao (approved 2026-02-23): Verified behavior against SUP-9821 reproduction steps. Approving; please ensure the feature gate is documented in the release notes.
release_notes: Add call sequencing policy for multi-tool calls, result hydration protocol v2, idempotency fingerprinting to reduce duplicate side-effects, and an opt-in OpenAI compatibility bridge. Opt-in feature via console flag or per-request header. Impact: safer parallel tool execution and more deterministic injection into model context.
notes_for_backport: No urgent backport required. If backporting for a managed customer, include the runtime HMAC key rotation utility (ENG-2463) and ensure feature gate defaults remain off.
